newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-US T-bond vols bid after late bond selloff.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-US T-bond vols bid after late bond selloff.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options bounced off early lows to end slightly firmer after underlying bond prices slid in late trade, traders said.
"Everything got bid up a little as the bonds sold off," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).

Traders were unsure what had caused the bond selloff. But they said there was rumor of a huge selling in 10-year notes, adding that the market was becoming somewhat nervous ahead of the July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, especially after making big gains earlier in the month.
September T-bond futures had been seesawing around 112 for most of the day, as they had been for days, and then tumbled to a low of 111-18/32 shortly before the close.
Implied volatilities for August and September T-bond futures options edged up about 0.1 point each on the day to around 8.0 and 8.3 percent respectively.
Earlier in the afternoon, volatilities softened in lethargic activity as bond prices clawed back up to Tuesday's closing levels after a fairly well received five-year Treasury note auction.
The Treasury's two-year-note auction on Tuesday was also perceived to be good.
The $11.5 billion five-year note auction today produced a high yield of 6.298 percent, at which 87 percent of the bids were awarded. Bid-to-cover ratio was a healthy 3.19 times.

"It seemed to be a pretty good auction but the market in general, I think, is in the process of relaxing from the recent highs until we get to the FOMC," said Brad Tyl, Aubrey G Lanston's CBOT floor manager. He characterized the activity in the past several days as "churning" and anticipated relatively minor fluctuations going into the FOMC meeting.

The market had met a near-term objective of 6.65 percent in the cash bond yield, where it had started falling on February's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, Tyl said.
Still, despite anticipation of subdued, consolidative trading in bonds, volatilities should uptick in the coming days because of the FOMC event risk, he added.
Among the biggest trades, one firm was said to have bought some 5,000 lots of September 110/108 put spread in a one-by-two ratio, while a bank was seen buying 1,000 of September 112-110 put spread.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Eurodollar volatilities were roughly unchanged as futures shed their midsession gains to end mostly flat.
December Eurodollar futures finished at just 0.005 point above Tuesday's close at 93.945 after briefly rising as high as 93.975, edging closer to the 93.995 June 13 high.
Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures options stood at 9.7 percent, little changed.
